record.paper_title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Multiple aperiodic levels for twisted geodesic flows
record.original_question: Does there exist a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic energy level? In other words, can a Hamiltonian system of magnetic-flow type on a twisted cotangent bundle have at least two distinct regular compact energy levels that carry no periodic orbits?

evidence.quote: This example has (Hamiltonian) analogues in all even dimensions; see [Gi6, Example 4.2].

Example 4.1 is the only known "naturally arising" example of a Hamiltonian flow with a regular compact aperiodic energy level. Furthermore, this is the only known example of a twisted geodesic flow with an aperiodic energy level. It is not known if there exists a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic energy level.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(N,g)$ be a closed Riemannian manifold, and let $\sigma$ be a closed 2-form on $N$ (a "magnetic field"). On the cotangent bundle $T^*N$, consider the twisted symplectic form $\omega_\sigma = \omega_0 + \pi^*\sigma$, where $\omega_0$ is the canonical symplectic form and $\pi : T^*N \to N$ is the projection. Let $H : T^*N \to \mathbb{R}$ be the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian $H(q,p) = \tfrac{1}{2}|p|_g^2$, and let $X_H$ denote its Hamiltonian vector field with respect to $\omega_\sigma$. The flow of $X_H$ is called a twisted geodesic flow (a magnetic flow). A regular compact energy level $\{H = c\}$ is said to be aperiodic if it contains no periodic orbits of $X_H$.

Question: Does there exist a twisted geodesic flow (i.e., a choice of closed manifold $N$, Riemannian metric $g$, and closed 2-form $\sigma$ on $N$) that possesses at least two distinct regular compact aperiodic energy levels?

artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any result constructing a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic regular compact energy level, nor any proof excluding this. The literature on the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture and magnetic flows discusses single aperiodic levels as the only known examples, and the question of multiple aperiodic levels in the twisted-geodesic setting does not appear to have been settled in publicly indexed sources.

status_evidence.title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the only known example of a twisted geodesic flow with an aperiodic energy level and lists multiple aperiodic levels as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of multiple aperiodic levels for twisted geodesic flows is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: A C^2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of Hamiltonian flows with aperiodic regular compact energy levels; does not address multiple aperiodic levels in twisted geodesic setting.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses single aperiodic levels but does not resolve the multiple-levels question for twisted geodesic flows.
